chunks: Some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: The reliable one narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
When two women testify for the owner of the right, along with his oath, then it is permissible.

key_terms.الثِّقَةُ: the reliable one — an unnamed but trusted narrator in the chain, a term used when the identity is withheld but reliability is affirmed
key_terms.جَائِزٌ: permissible/valid/allowed — used in fiqh to indicate legal validity of an action or claim
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحَقِّ: the owner of the right/the plaintiff — the one who holds a legitimate legal claim
key_terms.يَمِين: oath (yamin) — a sworn oath taken by the claimant to supplement witness testimony

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of two women combined with the plaintiff's oath valid in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a legal ruling from Imam Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the validity of testimony in judicial proceedings. The ruling specifies that two female witnesses combined with the plaintiff's own oath constitute sufficient evidence to establish a legal claim. This reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that two female witnesses, combined with the claimant's oath (yamin), are equivalent in evidentiary weight to one male witness with an oath, making the testimony legally valid.
